hints: Enqueue is the easy half: push onto B, done. All the thinking lives in dequeue.
Popping every element off B and pushing each onto F reverses them. A reversed LIFO is a FIFO - that single observation is the whole trick.
Only pour when F is empty. If you pour on every dequeue you get the right answers but ruin the running time, because elements move back and forth repeatedly instead of crossing once.

title: A queue built from two stacks
